For Applicant : Mr. Lukesh Kumar Mishra, Advocate (through virtual mode) For State : Mr. Keshav
Gupta, Govt.
Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 11/06/2024
1. Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 439 of CrPC for grant of regular bail.

First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with prayer for a direction to learned trial Court to expedite the trial.
2.

Applicant was arrested in connection with Crime No. 258 of 2023 registered at Police Station Gudhiyari, District - Raipur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of I.P.C.,
1860, and Section 4 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
3. Notice issued to complainant/victim is served upon father of victim, however, there is no representation on their behalf.
In the proceedings of first bail application also, no one appeared on behalf of complainant/victim even after service of notice.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18632 4.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent, he has not committed any offence as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the aforementioned crime.

After withdrawal of first bail application on 06.12.2023, victim as also her father along with some other witnesses have Aditya Sahu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134249742/
1 now been examined.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Victim in her statement has stated that she herself called applicant and with her own will she accompanied applicant.
Age of victim is disputed in evidence.

Before learned Trial Court, father of victim has stated that date of birth of victim to be 03.02.2004 and from the said date, on the date of incident, victim was a major girl and therefore, offence under POCSO Act will not be attracted.

He further contended that there are as many as twenty witnesses and till March,
2024, only seven witnesses were examined.
Trial may take some time for its hearing.
Applicant is in jail since 18.06.2023, therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicant.
He submits that allegation against applicant is of abducting and committing sexual intercourse with minor girl aged about 15 years.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

7. Taking into consideration facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation, submission of learned counsel for the parties, in particular, submission of learned counsel for applicant based on deposition of victim as also her father, period of Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18632 detention,
without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
8. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail, upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that - a) Applicant shall appear before the Trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
b) The applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
